question: Analyze June–July: where am I leaving money on the table and where do I risk going unsold?
lenses_active: L1 Money-leak · L2 Unsold risk · L3a Orphan night · L4 OTA parity
summary: June needs to be defended on price and "unstitched" on gap-nights; late July needs to be stimulated or accepted as fill-in. The last rooms of mid-June start at €320–344 with area demand still very high, while from late July the hotel is wide open at €184. One expensive night (Jun 23, €324) is lost because the following night is full.

charts.caption: Searches in the area (12 km) per check-in week. Demand drops from ~27,000 (mid-June) to ~6,800 (late July). Most requested stays: 2 nights (37,903) and 3 nights (32,908). Average lead time growing: 36 → 91 days. Destination data, not the hotel's own.

lenses.title: L1 — Money-leak · L3a — Orphan night
lenses.rule: Rule: last room at a rate with no premium, and free nights adjacent to full nights in a high-demand week.
lenses.note: The night of June 23 (€324) can't be sold as part of a 2-night stay because the 24th is full: a search for Jun 23→25 finds nothing. With demand concentrated on 2–3 nights, this is a lost sale on an expensive date.

lenses.title: L2 — Unsold risk
lenses.rule: Rule: low demand + many open categories + low price + inside the booking window.
lenses.note: Late July: area demand at its lowest, hotel wide open, price the lowest of the period (€184 vs €344 in mid-June). You're already past the average lead time: pickup is behind.

lenses.title: L4 — OTA parity (test stay Jun 19–21)
lenses.note: Parity respected on this date: direct isn't undercut by the OTAs. No action needed here.

date_map.heading: Date map
date_map.note: Coloring based on the availability calendar (sold-out) + sampled priced dates + demand curve. Not every single night was queried individually.

limits: This is an area-demand vs availability/price diagnostic, not a revenue management system. With SimpleBooking data alone it does not see: your actual on-the-books figures or pickup pace; real competitor rates (only OTA parity); an events source. Prices don't include any stay taxes. The pointers are conditional options ("if demand holds…"), not prescriptions.
events: You're full on these dates: Jun 24 and the cluster Jun 15–18, Jun 30, Jul 9–11. Can you confirm whether these are tied to events or fairs (so we can price accordingly in future years)? The skill detects the full dates but doesn't attribute the cause.
options: Check the floor on the last rooms of Jun 19–28.
Consider opening a 1-night stay on the orphan nights adjacent to the sold-out dates.
Decide whether to stimulate late July (short offer / package) or accept it as fill-in.
Turn on a scheduled scan that alerts when June's last rooms drop below threshold.
